question: Does the pinned parser reproduce the historical production-scale latency and memory result on the current frozen corpus?
hypothesis: A complete cache-reuse pass remains an order of magnitude slower than the retained structural full-rebuild build stage, with large files and LL fallback dominating parser cost.

config.processes: one fresh process per adapter repetition
config.pass: one parser instance per file; generated DFA caches persist within each repetition
config.strata: four equal-count strata ordered by source bytes

acceptance: The committed report contains no source text, original path, object name, credential, or absolute private path.
All 1,244 files are observed in every measured repetition.
Wall, parser core, phase totals, LL fallback count, diagnostics, and process peak RSS are reported.
Mean, sample standard deviation, coefficient of variation, and deterministic percentile-bootstrap 95% confidence intervals are retained.
Results are stratified into four equal-count byte-size strata.
limitations: Parser-only passes do not execute semantic extraction, persistence, or qualification.
The historical corpus had 1,237 files and 20,817,931 bytes; the current frozen corpus has 1,244 files and 20,944,414 bytes.
Three repetitions provide low-confidence bootstrap intervals.
The retained structural comparator is a broader full-rebuild build stage; comparing parser core against it is conservative, not phase-identical.
